summary: The legal length cap of 30 is too narrow for reliable runtime-class scaling across input-dependent recursive pruning. A direct count of cached interval states and split transitions verifies the required O(n^4) upper bound.

replacement_checks.evidence: A state is (first_start, second_start, size), giving O(n^3) possible cached interval pairs. Each state compares a fixed 26-letter inventory, may compare O(n) characters for exact equality, and tries at most O(n) split positions with O(1) cached child lookups, for O(n^4) total time and O(n^3) cache space.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover a swapped recursive decomposition, a false equal-length candidate, and the one-character base case; black-box real-test execution verifies the existing ordinary checks without inspecting their definitions.
